claims.text: Using Si as X in single-phase CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a continuous silicon-enriched chromium-oxide or silicate scale.
The scale formed on the Si-containing alloy has a thermal expansion coefficient closer to that of the underlying alloy.
Improved thermal-expansion matching reduces oxide/alloy interfacial stresses during high-temperature exposure.
Reduced interfacial stress inhibits oxide-scale cracking and spallation.
Mn- or Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form less-adherent and less-stable scales than the Si-containing alloy under similar conditions.
The protective surface mediator is a dense and coherent silicon-enriched chromium-oxide or silicate layer.
The silicon-enriched surface layer maintains intimate contact with the underlying alloy.
Si addition causes nucleation of a silicate phase.
The proposed silicate phase acts as a chemical barrier to oxygen ingress.
The proposed silicate phase reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between the scale and alloy.
Reduced thermal-expansion mismatch lowers interfacial energy and stress during thermal cycling.
Mn and Al do not promote formation of the proposed beneficial silicate phase.
Si-containing alloys will exhibit slower oxide-scale growth than Mn- or Al-containing comparison alloys.
The oxide scale on Si-containing alloys will remain coherent and intact during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
Mn- or Al-containing alloys will exhibit rapid oxide growth with frequent cracking and spallation.
Changes in temperature, atmosphere, or alloy microstructure may alter the proposed oxide behavior.
